extracted.intended_audience: applicants, agents and patent practitioners using the PCT system (international phase)
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive requirements and options governing international publication, Article 19 claim amendments, transmission of documents, and access to files during the PCT international phase, aimed at applicants and Offices processing international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Bureau publication availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the international application has been published, and the supplementary international search report has been received, it is made available for public inspection by the International Bureau on PATENTSCOPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published international applications and, where applicable, related reports are accessible electronically on PATENTSCOPE (https://www.wipo.int/patentscope/en/).

rubrics_metrics.name: Main procedural steps at the International Bureau
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Bureau monitors receipt of the record copy and notifies the applicant and authorities; receives Article 19 amendments filed by the applicant; publishes the international application (usually after 18 months from priority date); transmits copies of the application, international search report and written opinion (in form of IPR Chapter I) to designated Offices; issues IPR Chapter I if no Chapter II report has been established; transmits IPRs and translations to applicant and designated/elected Offices; and if a demand is filed, notifies elected Offices and transmits the IPR Chapter II and related documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is an ordered list of the main actions the IB performs; individual paragraphs in the Guide provide the details and timing for each step.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record copy receipt and notification
rubrics_metrics.description: The record copy of the international application should normally reach the International Bureau before the expiration of 13 months from the priority date; after receipt the IB notifies the applicant, the receiving Office and the International Searching Authority (unless it opts out) of the fact and date of receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Notifications are effected promptly after IB's receipt of the record copy. See paragraphs 6.057–6.058 for how the IB receives and monitors the record copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant action upon notification of record copy receipt
rubrics_metrics.description: The notification (Form PCT/IB/301) contains the list of designated Offices and allows the applicant to check exclusions or withdrawals; the applicant may withdraw designations at this point or any time prior to 30 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the notification to confirm designations (e.g., DE, JP, KR) and consider withdrawing designations if desired before the 30-month limit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entitlement and filing channel for Article 19 claim amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Article 19 the applicant is entitled to one opportunity to amend the claims in the international phase; any amendment under Article 19 must be filed with the International Bureau (not with the receiving Office or the ISA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Further amendment opportunities (including description and drawings) are available only under Article 34 upon filing a demand for international preliminary examination. Article 19 amendments must be in the language in which the application is published.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing limits for Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 19 amendments are available after the applicant has received the international search report and the written opinion, and remain available until the end of 16 months from the priority date or two months after the transmittal (date of mailing) of that report and opinion, whichever expires later. Amendments received after the time limit are still accepted if received before technical preparations for international publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the ISA declared under Article 17(2)(a) that no ISR would be established, Article 19 amendments are not allowed. If ISR exists but certain claims were found unsearchable under Article 17(2)(b), Article 19 amendments are allowed only for the searched claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contents of an Article 19 submission
rubrics_metrics.description: Submission of Article 19 amendments must comprise: (i) a complete set of claims in replacement of the original claims; (ii) a letter indicating the differences between the claims as filed and as amended plus the basis for the amendments; and (iii) an optional statement under Article 19.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All three elements (replacement claims, explanatory letter, optional statement) should be considered when preparing an Article 19 amendment to avoid later problems in Chapter II or national phases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format and numbering of replacement sheets
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement sheet(s) must contain a complete set of claims in replacement of the claims originally filed and must be accompanied by the explanatory letter. Replacement sheets should contain clean text only. All claims on replacement sheets must be numbered in Arabic numerals corresponding to claim order. If a claim is cancelled, no renumbering is required, but if renumbering is done it must be consecutive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an entire sheet is cancelled, the cancellation is evidenced only by the letter to the IB. Avoid mark-ups on replacement sheets.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents required in the accompanying letter
rubrics_metrics.description: The letter must indicate (a) the differences between the claims as filed and those as amended and (b) the basis for the amendments in the application as filed. For each claim the letter should state whether it is unchanged, cancelled, new, replaces one or more claims as filed, is the result of division of a claim as filed, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The basis for amendments must be given with specific references to parts of the original application (description, claims, drawings); non-specific indications such as “refer to the description as filed” are generally insufficient. Examples of suitable wording are provided in the Guide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language requirements for the accompanying letter
rubrics_metrics.description: The accompanying letter should be furnished in English or French. References may be made to the international application in the language of the international application where doing so will facilitate the examiner's locating the reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use English or French for the letter, but when necessary cite paragraph numbers or original-language excerpts to help the examiner find the basis for amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement under Article 19: content, form and limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Any amendment may be accompanied by a brief statement explaining the amendment and indicating any impact on the description and drawings; the statement is published together with the application. Statements not referring to a specific amendment are not permitted. The statement must not exceed 500 words if in English or when translated into English, must not contain disparaging comments on the ISR or citations, and must be in the language of publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: References to citations in the ISR may be made only in connection with a specific claim amendment. Failure to comply means the statement will not be published or communicated to designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification and distinctness of the Article 19 statement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Article 19 statement must be clearly distinguished from the accompanying letter and other statements; it must be headed “Statement under Article 19(1).”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the statement does not comply with requirements it will neither be published nor communicated to designated Offices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on adding new matter in Article 19 amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The PCT provides that amendments are not to go beyond the disclosure in the international application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement is not directly enforceable during Chapter I, but non-compliance may have adverse consequences during international preliminary examination and in the national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences if replacement sheets lack the required accompanying letter
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacement sheets filed with Article 19 amendments must be accompanied by a letter indicating the basis for the amendment. Substantive compliance is not checked during the international phase unless a demand for international preliminary examination is filed, but failure to comply may have adverse consequences during international preliminary examination and in the national phase.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the letter is included and adequately references the filed disclosure to avoid later issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing copies with the International Preliminary Examining Authority (IPEA)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a demand for international preliminary examination is filed, the applicant should file a copy of Article 19 amendments, the accompanying letter and the Article 19 statement (if any) with the IPEA with the demand or at the same time as the amendment is filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the IPEA requires a translation under Rule 55.2, furnish translations of the amendments and accompanying letter if you want them considered in international preliminary examination. The IB transmits copies to the IPEA if received prior to filing the demand, but filing directly with the IPEA avoids delay.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to use Article 19 amendments (strategic considerations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Because amendments under Article 19 are published with the international application, they may be useful to better define claim scope for provisional protection in designated States that provide such protection. However, if the applicant files a demand (Article 34) they can amend claims, description and drawings with the IPEA regardless of Article 19 amendments; therefore there is normally no need to use Article 19 when a demand is filed unless there is a specific reason, e.g., provisional protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether early public claim clarification (e.g., for provisional protection) outweighs possible disadvantages of publishing amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB does not publish the international application if: (i) no international filing date was accorded by the receiving Office; (ii) the application is considered withdrawn before technical preparations for publication completed; (iii) the applicant withdrew the application before technical preparations completed; (iv) at completion of technical preparations the only designated State remaining is the United States (Article 64(3)) unless exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check these conditions early if publication avoidance is desired.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and options for international publication
rubrics_metrics.description: International publication normally takes place promptly after expiration of 18 months from the priority date. An applicant may ask the IB for early publication; if ISR or the declaration under Article 17(2)(a) is unavailable at publication a special fee is payable. Publication normally occurs on Thursdays except when IB is closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early publication is possible but may incur a fee if ISR isn't available; publication schedule and fee details are in Annex B(IB).

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for changes before publication (technical preparations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical preparations for publication are completed by the 15th day prior to the date of publication. Changes to be taken into consideration for a specific publication date should reach the IB at least one day before the 15-day time limit (i.e., by Tuesday midnight CET for a Thursday publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit changes well before the 15-day technical-preparations cutoff to ensure incorporation; last day depends on publication weekday.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of the published international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication is electronic and will include any Rule 4.17 declaration and, if available, the international search report or the ISA declaration that no ISR will be established, and any amendment (including any Article 19 statement). If the time limit for amending claims has not expired, publication will carry an annotation; ISR or declaration published separately if received later. An international publication number (e.g., WO 2004/123456) is assigned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annotations will indicate pending items; later-received reports or amendments are published subsequently. Consult Article 21 and Rule 48 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication platform and front-page items
rubrics_metrics.description: On the date of publication the bibliographic data, title of the invention, the abstract and a characteristic drawing (if any) are made available on PATENTSCOPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bibliographic data and front-page items are the initial searchable elements available to the public on PATENTSCOPE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omission of information from international publication — criteria and process
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant can make a reasoned request (preferably Form PCT/IB/384) to omit certain information from publication, accompanied by replacement sheets (except where omission would remove an entire sheet) and a letter explaining why the information does not serve to inform the public, would clearly prejudice personal or economic interests, and that no prevailing public interest requires access. The request must be received before technical preparations for publication are completed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the IB finds the request satisfies the criteria it will omit the information and notify the applicant (Form PCT/IB/385); if not, IB will refuse (Form PCT/IB/386). IB will notify other Offices so they likewise do not make the omitted information public.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of international publication and translations
rubrics_metrics.description: If filed in Arabic, Chinese, English, French, German, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Russian or Spanish, the application is published in the filing language. Where publication is in a non-English language the IB prepares English translations of the title, abstract and the ISR (or Article 17 declaration) and includes them in the published application; the IB may prepare French translations where applicable. The applicant may propose an English translation of the title before 14 months from the priority date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Title and abstract (and translations) are published on PATENTSCOPE. Suggested translations submitted before 14 months may be considered in preparing IB translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication language when filed in other languages accepted by the ISA
rubrics_metrics.description: If filed in a language other than the listed publication languages but accepted by the ISA for international search, the applicant must furnish a translation into a language of publication accepted by the receiving Office; the application will be published in that translation language only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow paragraphs 6.020–6.023 for details on accepted languages and translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication language when filed in a non-accepted language
rubrics_metrics.description: If filed in a language which is neither a language of publication nor accepted by the ISA, the application is published in the language of the translation furnished by the applicant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure you provide the required translation so that publication can occur.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bilingual publication of bibliographic data on PATENTSCOPE
rubrics_metrics.description: Bibliographic data, titles and abstracts, and any figure on the front page of each published international application are published in English and in French on PATENTSCOPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PATENTSCOPE shows these key elements in both WIPO official languages for accessibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining copies of the published international application
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone may download the published international application from the WIPO website or order a copy from the International Bureau, preferably referring to its international publication number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Electronic access on PATENTSCOPE is the primary method; paper copies are available on request (subject to cost reimbursement where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to the published international application in electronic form
rubrics_metrics.description: The published international application in electronic form is available on PATENTSCOPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PATENTSCOPE is the IB's online portal for accessing published international applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obtaining copies of priority documents
rubrics_metrics.description: Third parties may apply to the Office with which the earlier application was filed, to certain designated Offices or to the IB for copies of priority documents. The IB makes copies of priority documents available after international publication on PATENTSCOPE or on paper upon request and reimbursement of cost, except where the international application was withdrawn prior to publication, or the priority claim was withdrawn or cancelled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check the status of the international application before requesting priority documents; withdrawn/cancelled priority claims may prevent IB from furnishing copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preventing international publication (withdrawal and timing)
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may prevent international publication by withdrawing the international application provided the notice of withdrawal reaches the IB before completion of technical preparations for publication (see technical-preparations cutoff). It is strongly recommended to send the notice directly via ePCT with strong authentication (use corresponding Action) to ensure immediate flagging. Alternative upload is available if ePCT cannot be used. A conditional withdrawal can be stated but may be ineffective if technical preparations are already complete. Non-payment of fees causing receiving Office declaration of withdrawal may have similar effect only if IB receives the declaration before technical preparations completion. Withdrawing the priority claim may postpone publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use ePCT Actions for secure and immediate effect. Be aware of the technical-preparations deadline; if passed, withdrawal will not prevent publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legal effects of international publication (Article 29 provisional protection)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 29 ensures, with qualifications, that provisional protection is available after international publication in the same way as after national publication of unexamined national applications. Qualifications allow Contracting States to make protection conditional on translations, expiration of 18 months from the priority date, and/or receipt by the designated Office of a copy of the published international application. Annexes indicate positions for each Contracting State.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check national/regional rules (Annexes) for conditions and whether provisional protection is available in a specific designated State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access at the International Bureau to file documents
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications filed before 1 July 1998 the applicant or authorized person may obtain copies of any document in the IB file (subject to cost); for applications filed on or after 1 July 1998 the IB makes certain documents available on PATENTSCOPE and will, on request but not before international publication and subject to Article 38, furnish copies of any document in its file (except information omitted from publication or public file access following a reasoned request).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests for copies are subject to reimbursement and confidentiality rules (see paragraphs 11.072–11.074).

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to the international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II) and related documents
rubrics_metrics.description: If requested by an elected Office, the IB makes copies of the international preliminary report on patentability (Chapter II) available on PATENTSCOPE to third parties, but not before the expiration of 30 months from the priority date. The IB also makes related documents received from the IPEA under Rule 71.1(b) available on PATENTSCOPE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some elected Offices have requested such access; consult IB lists (https://www.wipo.int/en/web/pct-system/texts/access_iper) to see which reports are made available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communication of copies to designated Offices and official notices
rubrics_metrics.description: The IB communicates a copy of the international application in the language of publication to each designated Office upon their request and at the time specified by that Office pursuant to Rule 93bis, but not prior to international publication. If the published language differs from the filing language, the IB will provide a copy in the filing language upon that Office's request. The IB sends notices after 19 months and after 28 months (Forms PCT/IB/308) informing the applicant of the Offices to which communication has been effected; these notices are conclusive evidence that communication took place on the specified dates.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On receiving the notices the applicant does not need to send copies to those designated Offices indicated as having been sent the communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early submission of copies to designated Offices (pre-publication transmittal)
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the international application may be communicated by the IB prior to the usual communication to any designated Office which requests it, but not before the expiration of one year from the priority date. The applicant may at any time transmit or ask the IB to transmit a copy to any designated Office (special transmittal by the IB requires payment of a fee). Such transmittal does not, unless expressly requested by the applicant, entitle the designated Office to start processing the application. If the applicant requests early commencement of national processing (under Article 23(2) or 40(2)), the IB will effect communication promptly upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special transmittal fees are indicated in Annex B(IB). Early communication needs to be requested and may not trigger national processing unless explicitly asked.
